title: J065--Philips Consolidated Service Agreement, Durham VAMC
description: Special Notice Special Notice Page 4 of 4 Special Notice *= Required Field Special Notice Page 1 of 4 INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Department of Veterans Affairs Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, on behalf of the Durham VA Medical Center intends to enter into a sole source procurement with Phillips Healthcare a division of Philips North America LLC, 414 Union Street, Philips Plaza 6th Floor, Nashville, TN 37219. NAICS code 811210-Electroinic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance. The proposed contract action is to provide a service agreement for Philips Radiology equipment at the Durham VAMC. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO FAR 6.103-1 using the procedures under RFO FAR 13.106-1 (b), Soliciting from a single source. Contract will be for a period of performance of 01 Dec. 2026 through 30 Nov. 2027. This notice of intent is not a request for quotation. Interested parties may identify their interest in the requirement and capabilities to monique.cordero@va.gov no later than 10:00 AM EST, Oct. 7, 2026. Telephone inquirers will not be accepted. All information shall be furnished at no cost or obligation to the Government. Gray market items are Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) goods sold through unauthorized channels in direct competition with authorized distributors. This procurement is for a service agreement for the Philips radiology equipment. No remanufacture or gray market items will be acceptable. Vendor shall be an OEM, authorized dealer, authorized distributor or authorized reseller for the proposed medical supplies, medical equipment and/or services contracts for maintenance of medical equipment (i.e., replacement parts), verified by an authorization letter or other documents from the OEM, such that the OEM s warranty and service are provided and maintained by the OEM. All software licensing, warranty and service associated with the medical supplies, medical equipment and/or services contracts for maintenance of medical equipment shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions. The delivery of gray market items to the VA in the fulfillment of an order/award constitutes a breach of contract. Accordingly, the VA reserves the right to enforce any of its contractual remedies. This includes termination of contract or, solely at the VA s election, allowing the Vendor to replace, at no cost to the Government, any remanufactured or gray market item(s) delivered to the VA medical facility upon discovery of such items. No solicitation will be made. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to complete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Q301--Reference and Esoteric Laboratory Testing
description: NO PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS ARE REQUESTED AT THIS TIME. THIS PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THE FORMAL RFP WILL BE POSTED AT SAM.GOV UNDER THIS NOTICE NUMBER 36C24227R0003 ON OR ABOUT 10/07/2026. OFFERORS ARE ENCOURAGED TO MONITOR SAM.GOV FOR THE FORTHCOMING RFP AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION. Brief Description of Services: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, on behalf of Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 2 South, intends to issue an RFP - Requirements Contract for comprehensive Reference Laboratory and Esoteric Testing Services. The contract will serve the VA Medical Centers listed in Appendix A. The contractor must provide everything needed to perform all required reference and esoteric laboratory testing. This includes, but is not limited to: All personnel, labor, equipment, transportation, information technology, supplies, and supervision Routine and STAT pickup and transportation of specimens from multiple VA medical facilities to the contractor s laboratory Pre-analytic processing and preservation of samples Performance of laboratory analysis as specified in the contractor s test manual and relevant standards Timely electronic and hardcopy reporting of results to ordering VA facilities, with direct system interface to the VA VistA Laboratory Information System (LIS) Consultation regarding test selection, specimen collection, result interpretation, and specimen requirements Provision of all consumables for specimen collection, preservation, and transport Maintenance of all required certifications and accreditations Compliance with HIPAA and VA information security requirements A complete Statement of Work, with all details and requirements, will be included in the final solicitation. Locations of Service (Appendix A): James J. Peters VA Medical Center VA New Jersey Healthcare System VA Hudson Valley Healthcare System VA New York Harbor Healthcare System Northport VA Medical Center Set-Aside: Unrestricted, this is not Set-Aside. NAICS: 621511 Medical Laboratories

title: AO Nestor 2027
description:
Groupe E utilise actuellement la plateforme ServiceNow comme outil central pour plusieurs processus internes et orientés clients. L’instance, nommée « Nestor », a été progressivement configurée pour répondre aux besoins opérationnels et organisationnels du Groupe.


ServiceNow sert notamment à la gestion des demandes métiers, offrant un portail centralisé et des workflows automatisés pour faciliter le traitement et le suivi des requêtes internes. La plateforme constitue également un pilier essentiel de l’ITSM, couvrant la gestion des incidents, des changements, des tâches et des problèmes.


Au-delà des processus internes, ServiceNow est utilisé pour la gestion des demandes clients, permettant une meilleure traçabilité, une amélioration de la qualité de service et un pilotage optimal des engagements (SLA). La solution intègre également un module dédié à la gestion du parc de véhicules, assurant le suivi opérationnel et administratif des ressources de mobilité du Groupe.

L’instance ServiceNow est aujourd’hui maintenue et évoluée par un partenaire externe, qui assure le support applicatif, les développements spécifiques et l’intégration technique, en collaboration avec les équipes internes de gouvernance.


Le contrat de licences ServiceNow et le contrat de services avec l’intégrateur arrivant à échéance, Groupe E lance cet appel d’offres afin d’assurer la continuité de ces services, d’optimiser les coûts et de garantir une évolution cohérente de la plateforme pour les années à venir.

title: Netherlands – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Rode lijst groene stip: effectiviteit natuurherstel
description: Dit onderzoek heeft tot doel de effectiviteit van gevoerde natuurherstelmaatregelen te evalueren, middels een gestandaardiseerde methodiek. De methode Rode Lijst met Groene Stip gebruikt Rode Lijst-soorten als graadmeter voor succes. Het idee is om deze methode nogmaals toe te passen, zodat een unieke tijdreeks ontstaat van 20 tot 30 jaar waarin de effecten van maatregelen nauwkeurig zijn gevolgd. De resultaten van het onderzoek moeten leiden tot: • Een overzichtstabel met daarin de effectiviteit van de verschillende maatregelen per soort(sgroep) en in de tijd; • Inzicht voor beheer en beleid voor welke soorten een maatregel effectief is; • Inzicht op welke termijn resultaten van een maatregel te verwachten zijn; • Inzicht na hoeveel jaar een maatregel herhaald dient te worden. Het maximale beschikbare budget voor deze opdracht bedraagt € 289.256,20 exclusief btw en € 350.000, - inclusief btw.

description: The United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) hereby gives notice of its intent to negotiate and award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order to: Company: Research Electronics International, LLC (REI) This procurement is conducted under the statutory authority of: FAR 13.106-1(b)(1) ("Soliciting from a single source" under Simplified Acquisition Procedures). USSOCOM requires specialized, field-deployable Technical Surveillance Countermeasures (TSCM), acoustic speech masking systems, radio-frequency (RF) spectrum analysis, and physical search instrumentation to support operational force protection, secure compartmented information facility (SCIF) sweeps, and counter-surveillance mission sets. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. A solicitation package will not be issued publicly. However, any interested party that believes it can manufacture or supply identical equipment, or demonstrate an equivalent technical capability that satisfies USSOCOM's operational requirements without causing unacceptable delay or cost duplication, may submit a written capability statement. Capability statements must include: Company Information: Legal company name, CAGE code, UEI number, business size status under NAICS 334515, and primary point of contact. Technical Details: Clear documentation demonstrating the ability to supply genuine OEM REI equipment or an alternative system that matches every form, fit, function, harmonic detection algorithm, and acoustic masking capability listed in Section 2. Response Deadline: All capability statements must be submitted via email no later than 10/7/2026 at 11:00AM Eastern Time. Primary Contact: Kristen Colyer, Contracting Officer kristen.colyer@socom.mil A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future.

description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (SSN) announcement. SSNs are issued to assist the Agency in performing market research to determine industry interest and capability. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this synopsis. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. Therefore, no proposals are being requested or accepted in response to this SSN. 1.0 Purpose In accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10, SSP is conducting market research to determine if sources are capable of successfully performing the requirements identified in this SSN. Specifically, SSP is seeking capable firms to execute the Shape Stable Nose Tip (SSNT) Manufacturing Capacity Expansion. This effort requires the Contractor to procure, install, integrate, and qualify specialized Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) and bespoke industrial manufacturing equipment necessary to support the entire lifetimes of the Mk7, Mk4B, and Mk21A strategic programs. The effort includes the phased procurement of Contractor-Acquired Property (CAP) including long-lead items, facility integration, execution of Installation Qualification, Operational Qualification, and Performance Qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) processes via the manufacturing of SSNT proofing billets, and Systems Security Engineering to achieve a Navy SSP Authority to Operate (ATO), as identified in Enclosure (1) SSN Statement of Work (SOW). The anticipated contract type will include Cost - No Fee Contract Line-Item Numbers (CLINs) for the physical equipment procurement, and Cost-Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) Level of Effort (LOE) CLINs for the installation, qualification, and engineering services. The Period of Performance (POP) will include a Base Year effort from 1 July 2026 � 30 September 2027, and two (2) corresponding one-year option periods extending through 30 September 2029. NOTE: Given the highly technical nature of SSP�s mission set as a major weapons systems command and corresponding technical requirements, respondents must provide recent and relevant past performance data (as detailed below) to demonstrate and substantiate the respondent�s ability to successfully execute requirements detailed in this SSN. 2.0 White Paper Capability Statement Credentials SSP is seeking detailed, complete, and thorough White Paper capability statements from interested firms who can demonstrate and document, with evidentiary support, that they 1) possess the minimum qualifications and experience identified in paragraph 3.0 which are critical to the successful execution of the requirements, and 2) demonstrate recent and relevant experience, as the Prime contractor (or subcontractor) performing the same/similar efforts of the same/similar scope, size, and complexity to the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements identified in paragraph 4.0. Interested firms must demonstrate their existing capability, or potential to acquire the capability, to meet the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements by the time of contract award, estimated to be 1 July 2027. 2.1 Small Business Concerns IAW FAR Subpart 19.2 Polices, SSP seeks to provide maximum practicable opportunities in its acquisitions to small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, HUBZone small business, small disadvantaged business, and women-owned small business concerns. If a small business concern intends to partner with another entity, the small business concern must identify which specific enclosure (1) SOW efforts/tasks it intends to perform, as well as the specific efforts/tasks the partner would perform, with the substantiating data required in this SSN supporting the identified partnering roles and responsibilities. NOTE: 100% of the enclosure (1) SOW and SSN requirements must be addressed in any submitted partnering submittal, if obtainable. NOTE: In the event this contract is set aside for small business concerns, the small business concern agrees that it will be in strict compliance and conformance with the percentage payment limitations for services, supplies, or construction (as applicable) to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities in accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting and state such in their response. 3.0 Minimum Qualifications / Experience Requirements Interested firms shall document and submit specific and evidenced / demonstrated possession of the minimum qualifications and experience requirements in the technical areas identified in bullets a through h below which are critical to the successful execution of the enclosure (1) SSN SOW requirements in paragraph 4.0. title: FEDLINK Serials Subscription Management
description: The Library of Congress, Federal Library and Information Network (FEDLINK) is conducting market research to identify potential commercial sources that may be able to provide serials subscription management & related support. The Government is contemplating a potential acquisition for the management & fulfillment of serial publications of all types and in all media, including but not limited to: traditional print materials that may be added to the physical holdings of a library or other institution, as well as electronic content hosted remotely by a publisher and related support and electronic access services. Subscription management includes all of the tasks necessary to activate, manage, and maintain both new subscriptions & the renewals of FEDLINK member agencies� subscriptions to serial publications, both print and electronic. These tasks fall into the following five critical areas: Ordering and renewing subscriptions Serving as a fiscal agent with publishers, including making timely prepayment and processing refunds Facilitating timely access to, and claiming delivery of ordered subscriptions, both print and electronic Troubleshooting and resolving end user access issues Providing reports and other administrative support for serials management. INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested entities are requested to provide capability statements or other documentation to demonstrate their ability to perform the contemplated requirements as described above. Responses should include, at a minimum: Company information, including company name, point(s) of contact, UEI, and CAGE code (if applicable) Subscription management capability: describe the entity's ability to manage large portfolios of serials subscriptions of various formats, including new subscriptions, renewals, cancellations, changes, and publisher relationship/coordination information Any other relevant information, such as commercial practices or capabilities, that the Government should consider when developing its acquisition strategy. This Notice is issued solely for market research purposes and is not a solicitation. No contract will be awarded a result of responses to this Notice. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this Sources Sought Notice, nor will the Government reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Interested parties should not submit proprietary, classified, or otherwise restricted information in their responses. Respondents are responsible for appropriately identifying such information contained in their submission. Responses should be limited to five (5) pages and must be submitted electronically to Kate Campbell, Contracting Officer, no later than 12:00pm Eastern time on Wednesday, October 7, 2026.

title: Z1DA--LOADING DOCK CONCRETE REPAIRS
description: The Central Virginia Health Care System (CVHCS) intends to solicit offers for construction services to repair and reconstruct the existing loading dock platform and stair system at the Richmond VA Medical Center, Richmond Campus. Work will include demolition of failed concrete, removal and replacement of damaged reinforcement steel, reconstruction of loading dock structural components, installation of new concrete and safety features, and application of protective concrete sealants. All work shall be performed per VA Design Guides, VA Master Specifications, OSHA 29 CFR 1926, and all applicable federal, state, and local regulations. Classification: Set Aside: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Program Set-Aside Product Service Code: Z1DA- Maintenance of Hospitals and Infirmaries NAICS Code: 238110- Poured Concrete Foundation and Structure Contractors Place of Performance: Central Virginia Health Care System 1201 Broad Rock Blvd. Richmond, VA 23249 Period of Performance: Approximately 90 calendar days from issuance of Notice to Proceed. Project Description: The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and expertise necessary to fully repair and reconstruct the loading dock platform stairs, treads, risers, reinforcement steel, and associated structural components. Scope includes demolition of damaged concrete, removal of deteriorated rebar, forming and reconstruction, installation of steel dowels and #4 reinforcement, placement of 3500 PSI concrete, installation of safety bumpers and yellow safety tread markings, broom finishing, sealing of repaired surfaces, and full compliance with VA and OSHA safety requirements. The contractor shall also ensure debris removal, barricading of work area, adherence to PPE protocols, proper delivery coordination, and compliance with all VA safety, structural, and life-safety requirements. Final acceptance will include a walkthrough with the COR and verification of compliance with VA structural safety standards. Solicitation Details: A Request for Quotes (RFQ) is contemplated in accordance with FAR Part 13. A response time of approximately 30 days is anticipated following issuance of the solicitation. This acquisition will be issued pursuant to FAR 36.204(b) Magnitude of Construction, which is estimated to be between $25,000 and $100,000. The solicitation, Statement of Work, wage determination, and all other applicable documents will be available electronically on SAM.gov on or about October 7, 2026. No email, fax, or telephone inquiries will be accepted as a result of this announcement. No additional information regarding scope, dates, or related details will be made available until issuance of the solicitation. A pre-bid conference/site visit will be announced in the solicitation; no additional site visits will be conducted. Once posted, it is the contractor's responsibility to review SAM.gov frequently for any amendments or updates. Contractor Registration Requirements: All interested contractors must be: Actively registered in SAM.gov Certified in SBA Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert) Current on VETS-4212 reporting, if applicable Current on online Representations and Certifications Registered under NAICS 238110 Notice to Offerors: The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation either before or after the closing date. If cancelled, the Government is not obligated to reimburse offerors for any costs associated with proposal preparation.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source to The MathWorks, Inc.
description: The Department of the Navy, Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific (NIWC Pacific), hereby publicizes its intent to negotiate and award a Firm-Fixed-Price modification to Contract N66001-26-P-6242 on a noncompetitive basis to The MathWorks, Inc. (CAGE 0C524), Natick, Massachusetts, pursuant to 10 U.S.C. ?????????????????? 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The proposed modification will add two one-year option periods for the continued provision of MathWorks enterprise software licensing, maintenance, and associated training in support of NIWC Pacific. The requirement includes enterprise licenses for MATLAB and Simulink software, associated MATLAB and Simulink toolboxes, extended software maintenance, and related training. The contemplated option periods are as follows: Option Item 0002 ??????????????????????????? Option Year 1 Enterprise Desktop Programs Manufacturer: The MathWorks, Inc. Quantity: 1 Period of Performance: 01 August 2027 ??????????????????????????? 31 July 2028 Option Item 0003 ??????????????????????????? Option Year 2 Enterprise Desktop Programs Manufacturer: The MathWorks, Inc. Quantity: 1 Period of Performance: 01 August 2028 ??????????????????????????? 31 July 2029. The proposed modification will establish the two option periods and associated pricing but will not exercise either option or obligate funds for the option periods at this time. Any future exercise of an option will be accomplished separately in accordance with the terms of the contract and applicable acquisition requirements. Based on the Governments market research and technical requirements, The MathWorks, Inc. is the only responsible source capable of providing the required MATLAB and Simulink enterprise licensing, associated toolboxes, maintenance, technical support, and training necessary to satisfy NIWC Pacifics minimum requirements. Market research considered other mathematical and scientific computing products and open-source alternatives, including Mathematica, Maple, GNU Octave, Scilab, SciPy, R, and Python. However, the Government did not identify an alternative that provides the combination of functionality, application-specific engineering capabilities, MATLAB/Simulink interoperability, documentation, technical support, and compatibility with NIWC Pacifics existing MATLAB-based environment necessary to satisfy the Governments current minimum requirements. Accordingly, the Government intends to negotiate the contemplated modification on a sole-source basis with The MathWorks, Inc.A redacted copy of the approved Justification and Approval (JA) supporting the use of other than full and open competition is attached to this Notice of Intent. This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive quotations, bids, or proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a quotation, proposal, or capability statement demonstrating their ability to satisfy the Governments minimum requirements. Any timely response received will be considered by the Government in determining whether another responsible source is capable of satisfying the Governments minimum requirements. This is consistent with the approved JA, which provides for publication through the Governmentwide Point of Entry and evaluation of timely capability information received from interested sources. A determination by the Government whether to compete the contemplated contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Point of Contact: Kylie Nevells Contract Specialist Email: kylie.m.nevells.civ@us.navy.mil All responding entities must be actively registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). To be considered for award, entities must possess an active Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code as part of their SAM registration. Capability statements, quotations, proposals, comments, or questions regarding this Notice of Intent shall be submitted via email to Kylie Nevells at kylie.m.nevells.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 07 October 2026 at 8:00 a.m. Pacific Time. This response deadline provides 15 calendar days from the date of publication of this notice. Telephone and fax inquiries will not be accepted. Responses received after the stated deadline may not be considered.

title: Chemistry CPRR with Laboratory Automation System IDIQ
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 08, in support of the Bay Pines VA Healthcare System, intends to award a single-award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the furnishing, installation, implementation, maintenance, and support of a fully integrated chemistry and immunochemistry laboratory automation system with a cost per reportable result pricing structure. The contractor shall provide all equipment, reagents, calibrators, controls, consumables, software, interfaces, accessories, labor, supervision, installation, implementation, training, preventive and corrective maintenance, technical support, and all other supplies and services necessary to furnish a complete, fully operational laboratory testing system in accordance with the Statement of Work. The proposed system shall support the clinical laboratory at the Bay Pines VA Healthcare System by providing high-throughput chemistry and immunochemistry testing, integrated laboratory automation, workflow optimization, specimen management, and interoperability with the existing laboratory information system and applicable third-party instrumentation. This acquisition will be conducted as a competitive procurement in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul Part 15. Award will be made using the best-value tradeoff process. Evaluation factors will include Technical Capability, Past Performance, and Price. Non-price Factors 1 and 2 are significantly more important than Factor 3 � Price. The Government intends to award one (1) IDIQ contract with a five-year ordering period, a guaranteed minimum of $15,000.00, and a maximum aggregate ordering ceiling of $45,000,000.00. The solicitation, including all attachments and any amendments is available electronically in SAM.gov. Interested offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for the solicitation, amendments, and other procurement-related information.

title: Shirley Creek Campground Improvements
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 127EAX26Q0114 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) to furnish all labor, materials, tools, transportation, and necessary supervision to perform campground improvements at Shirley Creek Campground, on the Brownstown Ranger District of the Hoosier National Forest. This project will develop individual campsites at the existing Shirley Creek Campground. Work includes staking camping spurs from plans, stripping turf, earthwork, excavating campsite spurs and social areas to sub-grade, install and compact aggregate base course, install and compact aggregate surface course, grading to ensure proper drainage around spurs and social areas, and restoring areas disturbed by construction operations with topsoil, seed and mulch. Stripped turf and excess earthen materials are to be disposed of, by the contractor, to on-site locations within the campground which will be designated by the COR. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 238910 The small business size standard is $19M This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Questions shall be submitted via email to christopher.malley@usda.gov and are due no later than September 28, 2026, at 1:00 PM Eastern Time. This will ensure enough time to respond before the solicitation period ends. Please include the solicitation name and number as the subject line of the email. Quotes shall be submitted electronically via e-mail to christopher.malley@usda.gov and pps.proposals@usda.gov and are due NLT October 7, 2026, at 1:00 PM Eastern Time.

description: Amendment 0002 � This amendment notifies industry that the required performance location will be expanded from the 100-mile radius to within a 250-mile radius of Crane, IN. Amendment 0001 � This amendment adds information on SAM.gov and JCP certification requirements needed for access to controlled attachments. This Sources Sought Notice is being issued by the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division (NSWC-CR) located in Crane, Indiana. NSWC-CR is conducting market research for vendors with the capabilities and facilities to provide Pier Side Support Equipment (PSSE) for the procurement of All Up Round + Canister (AUR + C) Upender for the loading and unloading of the Advanced Payload Module (APM). Efforts will include procurement of components and fabrication for APM Upending Fixtures (Drawing {Dwg.} # 8880357), AURC Upending Fixtures (Dwg. # 8939761), and APM Strongbacks (Dwg. # 8880354). The Government is requesting market information from industry for the services and supplies as described within. Naval Surface Warfare Center, Crane Division located at Naval Support Activity, Crane, IN intends to award this requirement as Commercial, Small Business Set-Aside, Firm-Fixed price (FFP), Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) with multiple award contracts (MAC) with a five-year ordering period. This sources sought notice is intended for planning purposes only and is issued solely for conducting market research in accordance with FAR Part 10. This does NOT constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP). The Government is NOT seeking or accepting unsolicited proposals. This notice shall NOT be construed as a contract, a promise to contract, or a commitment of any kind by the Government. If a solicitation is issued in the future, it will be announced via the SAM.gov website, and interested parties must comply with that announcement. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or information provided as a result of this sources sought notice. Response Requirements: General. All interested parties are encouraged to submit company and product literature, a white paper no longer than 10 pages to the Contract Specialist, Maggie Riser, margaret.j.riser.civ@us.navy.mil, by the closing date and time of this sources sought notice. The subject field of the email should contain �APM/AURC MAC RFI Response.� Responses should provide sufficient detail for assessment of potential contracting strategies and company interest. Failure to provide a response does not preclude participation in any possible future RFP, if issued. Please be advised that all submissions in response to this sources sought notice will become Government Property and will not be returned. Submitters should properly mark their responses with appropriate restrictive markings. Information that is proprietary or competition sensitive will be protected from disclosure under the public records law only if properly labeled as such. Specific responses to the approaches will not disqualify or have an impact on participation and evaluation on future solicitations. Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing via e-mail to the Contract Specialist�s email address. Verbal questions will not be accepted. title: ARPA-H Comprehensive Organ System Modeling in Outer Space (COSMOS) Innovative Solutions Opening
description: The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) Comprehensive Organ System Modeling in Outer Space (COSMOS) Initiative aims to definitively prove or disprove if exposure to microgravity in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) truly accelerates tissue aging across brain, cardiac, uterine, and kidney tissue types and across several adult age brackets. Provided Tissue Aging Rate in Space (TARIS) exceeds Tissue Aging Rate on Earth (TAROE) at a rate that exceeds the on Earth breakeven cost for new drug R&D, COSMOS will create a first-in-class platform for fully autonomous, high-throughput drug screening in LEO that would be more cost effective and faster than new drug R&D on Earth. ARPA-H anticipates multiple Other Transaction awards resulting from this announcement. title: Title: Industry Day for Beneficial Use of Dredge Material at Piney Island, MCAS Cherry Point, NC
description: Title: Industry Day for Beneficial Use of Dredge Material at Piney Island, MCAS Cherry Point, NC The Industry Day Meeting is for a potential beneficial use project at Piney Island located in Carteret County, NC. The project work would be included as an Option in the next planned AIWW Maintenance Dredging Contract, which will be solicited sometime in late Spring / early Summer 2027.Project Description: The Piney Island Beneficial Use of Dredged Material project involves placing approximately 8,000 cubic yards of dredged material across 9.3 acres of degraded brackish marsh at the northern tip of Piney Island, targeting a final elevation of 1.15 feet NAVD88 (plus or minus 0.25 feet, capped at 1.4 feet NAVD88). Two sediment sources within the Wilmington Districts navigation maintenance program are under consideration, including the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway (AIWW), specifically Core Creek reaches, and Wainwright Slough, a shallow draft navigation channel in the vicinity of the project. The placement site is roughly 12 to 15 miles from the potential dredging areas, and all sites are located in northern areas of Carteret County, NC (see attached overview map). The project work is proposed to be included in the next planned Wilmington District Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway maintenance dredging contract, which will be solicited in late Spring / early Summer 2027.The Industry Day Meeting will be held on 7 October 2026 at 1:00 PM EST via Teams. In addition, breakout sessions will be provided with individual contractors following the group industry day meeting. Please indicate with your RSVP if you would like to request a breakout meeting. Please RSVP no later than 3PM ET 2 October 2026 to both Jenifer Garland and Sonny Smith at jenifer.m.garland@usace.army.mil and sonny.z.smith@usace.army.mil if you plan to attend the Industry Day and/or request a breakout session. A Teams calendar invite will be sent out to all RSVP.

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. The intended contract is a firm-fixed price. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20, is conducting market research to identify potential sources which can provide the following in support of the VA Portland Healthcare System (VAORHCS), Portland, Oregon. VAPORHCS has a need for a base plus two (2) option year contract for licensing and service for MRI and CT Circle CVI42 postprocessing software. Please see the next 2 pages for requirement details. Vendor shall be an OEM, authorized dealer, authorized distributor, or authorized reseller for the proposed equipment/system, verified by an authorization letter or other documents from the OEM. All software licensing, warranty and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions. For set-asides: Please indicate in your response whether they can comply with VAAR 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting and/or FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting (e.g., will not pay more than 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities) should a set-aside be considered. Full text of clauses can be found here: 852.219-75, VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting: https://www.va.gov/oal/library/vaar/vaar852.asp#85221975 FAR 52.219-14: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide/far-overhaul-part-52#FAR_52_219_14 Potential candidates having the capabilities necessary to provide the stated services at a fair and reasonable price are invited to respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail to Jennifer Robles at jennifer.robles1@va.gov no later than October 7, 2026, 1PM, Mountain Time. No telephone inquiries will be accepted. RESPONSES SHOULD INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION: Company name, address, SAM UEI, and business size; point of contact name, phone number, and e-mail address; whether supplies/services are presently offered on a current GSA Federal Supply Schedule contract, NASA SEWP, or any other Federal contract. If offering a system with similar physical characteristics, please include business size of manufacturer for Non-Manufacturer Rule (NMR) determination. NAICS Code 541519, 150 employees, is applicable to determine business size standard. Any questions or concerns may also be directed via email to Jennifer Robles at jennifer.robles1@va.gov. REQUIREMENT INFORMATION 1. Background. The Portland VA Medical Center (PVAMC) requires licensing and service for MRI and CT Circle CVI42 postprocessing software. 2. Scope. All service and support are to be performed on the software hosted at PVAMC and utilized in the Radiology Department. Service may be performed remotely via telephone 3. Specific Tasks. Vendor to provide licensing for the following- Cardiac MR Software for function, flow, angio, and tissue mapping Coronary Vessel and Calcium Scoring Licensing All labor and travel shall be included. All technicians shall be trained by Circle Cardiovascular 4. Performance Monitoring. The tasks are well defined and can, therefore, be easily monitored by the Government point of contact (POC), who shall represent the government for this process. The contractor performance will be monitored and the work certified by the POC. The POC will assure contractor quality by routine inspections, product sampling, and monitoring of work while work is being performed. 5. Security Requirements. All contractors will be escorted by a VA employee. All contractors shall check in and out with Biomedical Equipment Support Specialist or designee in 1D106-100-p 6. Other Pertinent Information or Special Considerations. The contractor shall provide service engineers that have specialized experience with Circle CVI42 systems. The contractor s services engineers must be original equipment manufacturer (OEM) trained on the software, and have a valid training certificate that is kept up to date. The contractor s service engineer shall have fast access to troubleshooting and ability to elevate troubleshooting assistance, and regional support. 7. Inspection and Acceptance Criteria. The POC is responsible for certifying that the work done under this contract is performed to standard. The POC is also responsible to assure the inspection and acceptance of products provided incidental to services. 8. Place of Performance. Work will primarily be performed at the VAPORHCS or at place designated by vendor for remote support 9. Period of Performance. Base: 12/20/2026 - 12/19/2027 OY1: 12/20/2027 - 12/19/2028 OY2: 12/20/2028 - 12/19/2029 10. Delivery Schedule. title: Synopsis for Oil Water Separator Cleaning Maintenance
description: This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice published for informational purposes only; no formal solicitation is currently available. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) � Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), Washington, anticipates issuing a solicitation for Oil Water Separator (OWS) cleaning and maintenance services. The purpose of this requirement is to establish an Requirements contract to provide all personnel, equipment, containers, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and non-personal services necessary to perform comprehensive OWS maintenance at JBLM. The contractor shall ensure OWS systems function as designed to prevent the discharge of contaminants, oils, and hazardous materials into the environment. Performance requires the scheduled removal and proper disposal of sediment, sludge, and contaminated water. These services directly support the mission readiness of military and civilian operations at JBLM by maintaining critical infrastructure in full compliance with federal, state, and local environmental regulations, including the Clean Water Act and Washington State Department of Ecology standards. The contract will consist of a base period and four (4) one-year option periods, commencing on or about 1 June 2027. As requirements develop, the Government will issue Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task orders on an as-needed basis in accordance with an established Price List. The Government anticipates releasing the solicitation between mid-October to early November 2026, with an open response period of approximately 30 days. The solicitation, attachments, and technical exhibits will be distributed exclusively through the Contract Opportunities section of the System for Award Management at SAM.gov; no paper copies will be provided. To be eligible for award, prospective contractors must maintain an active registration in SAM under NAICS code 562998 (All Other Miscellaneous Waste Management Services). title: SOURCES SOUGHT � IDIQ Contract for Wood Utility Poles
description: UPDATE: This notice has been revised to request industry feedback on establishing freight prices at contract award, clarify contractor unloading requirements, update the delivery location attachment, and include a list of the wood pole CLINs. SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE � IDIQ Contract for Wood Utility Poles The Western Area Power Administration (WAPA) is conducting market research to identify qualified businesses capable of furnishing and delivering treated Pacific Coast Douglas Fir wood utility poles in accordance with the attached specifications and drawings. The Government anticipates establishing a Firm-Fixed-Price IDIQ contract with a three (3) year ordering period. Orders will be issued on an as-needed basis. Delivery locations include various WAPA facilities throughout the Upper Great Plains, Rocky Mountain, Desert Southwest, and Sierra Nevada Regions as listed in Attachment C. The contractor would be responsible for unloading poles into WAPA storage bunks. Truck-mounted or separate unloading equipment would be acceptable, provided all necessary personnel and equipment are present and ready when the delivery arrives. Transportation and unloading would be included in the freight price. This notice is for market research purposes and will be used to determine the availability of qualified small business concerns, the potential for a small business set-aside, and the appropriate acquisition platform. Interested firms are requested to provide the following information: Company name, UEI, and CAGE code. Business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 321114 (550 employees). Indicate whether your firm is the manufacturer/treater of the wood poles or a distributor/dealer. If you are a distributor/dealer, identify the specific manufacturing/treating mill(s) that will produce the poles, and confirm whether that manufacturer is a small business (under 550 employees). Confirmation of ability to meet the attached specifications, drawings, and contractor unloading requirements described in this notice across all four WAPA regions. Indication of whether your firm holds an active GSA Schedule contract with these utility poles on your approved pricelist (if applicable, provide contract number and SIN). Brief description of relevant past experience providing similar wood utility poles. Freight pricing approach. WAPA is considering establishing freight prices at IDIQ award that would apply to subsequent delivery orders, subject to a defined economic price adjustment mechanism. Freight prices would include transportation and contractor unloading at the delivery locations. Routine delivery would be required within 12 weeks after order issuance. Please briefly address: One approach under consideration is a freight price per pole, by pole CLIN and delivery location. Can your firm support this approach? Identify any concerns or recommended changes. Could particular pole CLINs or delivery locations share freight rates? If so, identify the suggested groupings and any limitations. How should smaller orders be priced without unnecessarily increasing freight prices for large orders? Historical examples reviewed generally involved mixed pole lengths and 20 or more poles per destination, although smaller quantities, particularly of longer poles, may be required. These examples do not establish a minimum order quantity. What objective index or other adjustment method would you recommend for freight prices over the three-year ordering period, considering the transportation methods your firm would use? Responses shall be emailed to tthomas@wapa.gov no later than October 7, 2026 at 3:00pm MT. This notice is for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred in responding to this notice. Please do not submit pricing information

title: TRAVEL SERVICES FOR NON-FEDERAL PEER REVIEWERS
description: Introduction This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. An organization that is not considered a small business under the applicable NAICS code should not submit a response to this notice. The applicable NAICS code for this acquisition is 561510 � Travel Agencies, with a small business size standard of $22.0M. Background The National Institutes of Health (NIH) is one of the world�s largest biomedical research organizations and is the focal point for funding medical research. The Center for Scientific Review (CSR) is the portal for NIH grant applications and is the central receipt point for most Public Health Service applications. As such, CSR is responsible for assigning applications it receives to scientific review groups for scientific review to funding components for award considerations. CSR also carries out peer review for the majority of research and research training applications submitted to NIH. The Scientific Review Evaluation Activity (SREA) Management and Service Center (MSC) coordinates review activities for the Center for Scientific Review (CSR). The SREA MSC is a key component of the NIH extramural biomedical research program, providing centralized administrative and operational support for the scientific peer review process. This support includes coordinating approximately 1,700 peer review meetings annually, supporting the review of approximately 92,000 grant applications each year, and providing administrative and travel support for approximately 28,000 domestic and foreign scientific non-federal reviewers annually. Because grant applications must be processed within very specific time frames, to avoid missed funding opportunities by researchers, flexibility in travel support services is essential. Travel tickets and travel support services must meet the NIH timeframes and coincide with the high demand of volume. Purpose and Objectives The specific objective of this requirement is to provide a range of travel support services to the NIH Scientific Review Evaluation Activities Management and Service Center (SREA MSC), which supports the centralized NIH peer review process through the Center for Scientific Review (CSR). These services include, but are not limited to, issuing airline, bus, and train tickets and providing reporting, invoicing, and billing services in accordance with SREA and NIH requirements. Project requirements The Government requires travel management support services for Non-Federal Peer Reviewers participating in NIH grant application review meetings, facilitated by the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) and the Scientific Review and Evaluation Award (SREA) Meeting Support Contract (MSC). The Contractor shall provide comprehensive transportation and ticketing support, including but not limited to the following capabilities: Volume and Scope Process an estimated average of 4,240 travel transactions per month (based on peer review Council Round cycles), including airline, rail, and bus tickets. Arrange and issue coach-class, non-refundable, direct round-trip electronic tickets at the lowest available fare, in compliance with applicable NIH/SREA travel guidelines and the Fly America Act for international travel. Financial Capacity Maintain a minimum line of credit of $12,000,000 with corporate banks to sustain travel costs without use of a government credit card, and to carry receivables beyond 90 days pending Government reimbursement. Service Continuity Demonstrate the ability to provide uninterrupted, 24/7 continuity of service, including after-hours and emergency support (e.g., power outages, national emergencies, weather events), for travelers en route or within 12 hours of scheduled departure. Roster Management and Data Security Securely receive and process daily authorization rosters transmitted via secure FTP from NIH's electronic Research Administration (eRA) system. Verify traveler authorization and associate reviewer, meeting, and transaction data for billing and reporting purposes. Protect the confidentiality of all personally identifiable information (PII) and comply with applicable Federal privacy and data security requirements. Customer Service Respond to routine inquiries within 24 hours (sooner for urgent matters). Acknowledge and resolve complaints within established timeframes. Maintain trained staff knowledgeable in NIH travel policies. Reporting and Booking System Provide a secure, authenticated reporting application, typically via Global Distribution System (GDS) integration, capable of supporting at least 500 registered users with up to 20 simultaneous users. Support data export in standard file formats (.csv, .xls, .xlsx) for financial reporting and reconciliation. Anticipated period of performance The Government anticipates awarding a single award IDIQ contract, featuring a one-year Base Period and four one-year Option periods, under which firm-fixed price task orders may be placed. The options periods may be unilaterally exercised by the Government. If the Government elects to exercise these options, the Contractor shall provide the resources as stated above. Capability statement/information sought Small business concerns that believe they possess the capabilities necessary to perform the required work should submit a comprehensive capability statement to the Contracting Officer. The capability statement must address each project requirement individually and specifically demonstrate the organization�s ability to satisfy those requirements. At a minimum, the capability statement should include the following: The Contractor must demonstrate the capability, competence, and experience necessary to provide high-volume travel support services for both domestic and international travel. Total Number of Employees: Provide the total number of employees within the organization. Personnel Qualifications: Describe the professional qualifications, experience, and expertise of key personnel as they relate directly to the requirements outlined in this notice. Relevant Experience: Provide a description of the organization�s general and specific past performance and experience relevant to the anticipated requirements. Similar Research and Projects: Identify previous research efforts, projects, or contracts that are similar in scope, scale, and complexity to the anticipated requirements and describe the role of the organization and proposed personnel in those efforts. Confirm your firm's ability to support weekly billing reconciliation processes. All electronic and information technology (EIT) used under this contract must comply with Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act, as implemented by the Access Board's accessibility regulations (36 CFR part 1194). More info: https://www.section508.gov/. Confirm your firm's ability to comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements for all electronic documents and IT systems delivered under this contract. Page Limitations: Interested qualified small business organizations should submit a tailored Capability Statement not to exceed 5 pages, excluding resumes. Capability Statements must not include links to internet web site addresses (URLs) or otherwise direct readers to alternate sources of information. Font size must be 10

title: Parachute Packing Press
description: This effort is for the procurement of (1) Parachute Packing Press Model GSU-449/E (PN: COM00150-1; NSN: 1670-99-555-6604) for the F/A-18 Kuwait Classic program. Under authority 10 U.S.C.2304(c)(1) and implemented in FAR 6.302-1(b)(1)(i), this authority shall be used when the program needs can only be satisfied from only one source with unique capabilities. Any attempt to procure a different part number would require the Government to fund a Preliminary Design Review (PDR) Critical Design Review (CDR) First Article Test (FAT) and Test & Evaluation (T&E) effort for a new vendor. The Government would have to fund personnel to be on the Source Selection Team to review proposals. Any change in form, fit or function would require changes to the existing Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) (technical publications, spares inventory, calibration) which would incur additional costs for update in the amount of $200,000 to $250,000. The process required to obtain an alternate asset is cost-prohibitive and would force the FMS Partner to utilize an asset that is not supported, compatible or interchangeable with the USN-approved configuration. This requirement will be processed under the authority FAR 6.302-1(b)(1)(i), whereby only one source with unique capability can supply the requested item. Market Research was performed by the Lakehurst Technical team. The Original Equipment Manufacturer of these items is Allied Defense Industries | Cage 0GD25. The US Government does have some technical data rights (e.g., drawings), but is unable to compete this request due to specific proprietary items to Eaton within the design of the end item. Acquisition Method Code: 3H - acquire directly from the manufacturer/US GOV does not have sufficient data. No additional market research was conducted for the reasons discussed above, and as such, it is the Governmnt's intention to conduct the repair procurement on a sole-source basis to Allied Defense Industries | Cage 0GD25.

title: Department of Navy Rapid Capabilities Office Disruptor Day: Multi-Sensor Data Fusion & Analytics for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA)
description: I. INTRODUCTION This Special Notice announces the Department of Navy Rapid Capabilities Office (DONRCO) Disruptor Days. The purpose of this event is to provide industry access to unique Government assets (test ranges, Labs, equipment, data) to support the development of mission-critical solutions. This initiative explicitly highlights a strategic partnership between Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) and Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI). PAE MS will serve as the primary evaluators, and the ONI will be actively involved throughout the planning, evaluation, and review process to ensure solutions meet rigorous operational demands. Disclaimer: This announcement does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. Any submission of information is strictly voluntary. II. TOPIC DESCRIPTION Globally significant maritime chokepoints present dense, asymmetrical, and highly dynamic threat environments. To address these operational challenges, the DONRCO seeks to identify and evaluate commercial data and technologies capable of performing rapid data fusion and multi-sensor correlation to support real-time Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA). Technical Focus The Department of the Navy (DON) needs to detect, locate, identify, and track all maritime vessels. The DON needs data solutions that can follow all types of vessels, from cooperative ships that report their location (self-reporting vessels) to non-cooperative "dark targets" that try to hide their positions. Dark targets may be involved in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, illicit drug trafficking, illegal arms trafficking, terrorism activities, or piracy. The DON is interested in novel data sources and analytics tools that can plug into and enhance the DON�s unclassified MDA tool, called SeaVision (https://info.seavision.volpe.dot.gov/). This event will experiment with novel combinations of data and analytics tools to demonstrate improvements in analytical MDA results by showing: the direct output of vessel positions, types, and predicted tracks. For this Disruptor Day event, data provided by participants should be in GeoJSON format. Data provided to participants for analysis will also be in GeoJSON format. Innovative Industry Solutions Submissions and demonstrations will focus on the following key operational and analytical capability areas. Participants can demonstrate in one or both capability areas. 1. Novel Data Sources After registration, the DON will specify a preferred location and window of time for data collection so that different data sources can be most easily overlaid with baseline SeaVision data. Advanced Data Solutions: Participants could demonstrate novel, previously untapped information pipelines to feed MDA analytical tools. High-Granularity Insights: Participants could demonstrate precise entity resolution and deep tracking capability. Latency and Timing: Participants should provide information regarding latency of data collected as well as how often data can be collected. 2. Novel Analytics Tools Correlation Engines: Participants could demonstrate automated calculators or AI tools to rapidly identify and report hidden relationships across disparate datasets. Source Identification: Participants should include identification of all data sources used to generate analytical results (e.g., a specific Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image, Automatic Identification (AIS) data feed, or Radio Frequency (RF) signal). Methodology Description: Participants should provide a high-level description of the analytic process or algorithms used. This information must be sufficient for the DON to understand the methodology, verify its legitimacy, and assess effectiveness during operational use. In-Scope Data Sources for Both Capability Areas New data sources and platforms must be capable of supporting the possibility of ingestion, correlation, and analysis using a standardized GeoJSON format. In addition to the following data types, vendors are encouraged to propose data sources beyond this list and/or ways to enhance these data types with additional attributes or analytics provided in GeoJSON format: Electro-Optical (EO) imagery and intelligence data, Infrared (IR) data and thermal imaging feeds and RF data, including signal emissions, intercept feeds, and spectrum analysis tools. SAR imagery and processing tools. Commodities Data (e.g., cargo manifests, shipping declarations, port-of-origin records, global trade statistics). Other Data (social media, acoustics, etc.) III. EVENT DETAILS The Disruptor Days event will occur starting the Week of November 30, 2026 (with a planned 2-week testing window) at NIWC Pacific in San Diego, CA. The event will take place in a specialized laboratory environment that allows vendors to brief their products in a traditional industry day format and execute live analytical evaluations. The DON anticipates using Limited Purpose Cooperative Research and Development Agreements (LP-CRADAs) to support this effort. More detailed information to follow. Following the event, selected vendors will receive structured feedback and scoring performance summaries from the Government evaluation panel. IV. REGISTRATION To Register for the Maritime Domain Awareness Disruptor Days, interested vendors should submit their information here: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/PaVKy9YV3S Additionally, DONRCO will host a virtual Q&A session prior to the event to answer vendor questions. Attending the virtual Q&A Session is optional and not required for Disruptor Day registration. Registration via the above form also serves to sign up for the Virtual Q&A session. Virtual Q&A session will be held: 1300 EDT, Wednesday, September 30, 2026 Sign-up Deadline for the Virtual Q&A session: 1200 EDT, on September 29, 2026 Pre-registration is REQUIRED for both the virtual Q&A and the Disruptor Days event. No walk-ins will be permitted. A downs selection will occur depending on interest due to limitations of space and time constraints. Additional information will be required prior to final event registration. V. SIGNIFICANT DATES AND TIMES Event / Milestone Date & Time Special Notice Announcement Released 18 September 2026 Virtual Pre-Event Q&A Sign-Up Deadline 1200 EDT on 30 September 2026 Virtual Pre-Event Q&A Session 1300 EDT on 1 October 2026 Final Survey Submission Closes 1600 EDT on 9 October 2026 Attendance & Invitation Approvals Sent 16 October 2026 Technical Q&A Session (Data Sharing & Setup) 21 October 2026 Disruptor Week Event Begins (NIWC Pacific, San Diego, CA) Week of 30 November 2026 (2-Week Duration) Disruptor Day Distinguished Visitor Day (NIWC Pacific, San Diego, CA) 10 December 2026 VIII. POINTS OF CONTACT Any questions regarding this announcement, data integration requirements, or event logistics should be submitted via email to: DisruptorDay@us.navy.mil

title: Jet Propellant Thermally Stable (JPTS) Transportation Services
description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy intends to solicit for contractor-provided transportation and logistical support services for the movement and delivery of JPTS aviation fuel utilizing contractor-furnished containers, trucks, and related equipment. Contractor-furnished containers must be certified for JPTS transportation, have an approximate capacity of 24,000 liters (6,340 gallons), and be equipped with appropriate fueling connections, pumps, and adapters. The requirement includes container cleaning and inspection compliance, staging and transportation operations, delivery coordination, loading and offloading support, shipping documentation, customs clearance support, and associated logistics management necessary to transport fuel from the designated port location to Government storage facilities.

REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. title: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) (Expressions of Interest and Request for Information)
description: THIS IS AN EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (EOI) AND REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. No solicitation is available. This notice is released pursuant to FAR Part 10 and FAR 15.201, Exchanges with Industry, for the purpose of conducting market research. The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is currently in the pre-solicitation phase for a contractor to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE). DOE expects to award a new contract during the last quarter of fiscal year 2027 which is expected to include a 60-day transition period. ORISE is a DOE Office of Science (SC) asset dedicated to enabling critical scientific, research, and health initiatives of the Department and its laboratory system. The ORISE mission is to develop people and solutions to strengthen our nation�s competitive advantage in science. ORISE focuses on scientific initiatives to develop the next generation of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) professionals through education and research participation programs; promote and elevate the quality of DOE funded research by facilitating peer and merit reviews; facilitate the Department�s Institutional Review Board (IRB) and Human Subjects Working Group activities, providing information on long-term health outcomes from current and former workers; ensure readiness and respond to radiation medical emergencies through the operation of the Radiation Emergency Assistance Center/Training Site (REACT/S); and provide independent assessment and verification for environmental cleanup, thus enabling DOE�s protection of workers and the public. The purpose of this notice is to (1) request expressions of interest from interested parties and (2) request information from interested parties regarding perceived barriers to competition associated with this acquisition. This market research will assist SC with identifying and minimizing barriers to competition, identifying and mitigating risks, and identifying appropriate Request for Proposals (RFP) terms and conditions. Responses to this notice should include the following information as appropriate and applicable: Prospective offerors business name, including parent and member organizations Point of contact, including a telephone number and an email address Business size (e.g., large, small, 8a, etc.) Nature of proposing entity (e.g., joint venture, limited liability corporation, etc.) Interest as being either a prime or subcontractor The Department may utilize the EOI�s received in response to this notice to publicize a list of parties interested in this acquisition. Indicate whether or not you would like to be included on a list of interested parties made available to the public. Your organization will not be listed unless you furnish your agreement. If agreement is provided, unless otherwise noted, the published list will include the prospective offeror�s name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, and interest as being either a prime or subcontractor. Brief description of your capabilities Due to the preliminary stage of this acquisition, only a draft Statement of Work (SOW) is currently available, which is attached for information only. Please review and identify sections of the SOW that may give your business pause in responding to a subsequent RFP. Provide suggestions on how the assessment criteria for such sections could be structured to make your business more competitive. Describe any other concerns you perceive as barriers or significant risks that would prevent qualified companies from submitting a proposal to a subsequent RFP. Based on the concerns identified above, describe any suggestions that could help mitigate those perceived barriers or significant risks. Also, describe any perceived barriers or significant risks you might perceive as too difficult to reasonably mitigate (if any). Identify any information that would be pertinent to provide to interested parties to promote a better understanding of the requirements. All interested parties are invited to submit a response to this notice. Interested parties are not required to respond to all items. Submissions can include responses to one or all of the items above. While there is no specific format required, responses should be no more than five (5) pages with a font no smaller than size 12. Responses should be submitted to ORISEcompetition@doe.gov. The subject of the email should read �EOI / RFI�. Submissions in response to this notice do not commit an interested party to submit a proposal, nor does failure to submit a response preclude an interested party from submitting a proposal. Responses should be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on October 7, 2026. DOE reserves the right to use any and all information submitted by, or obtained from, an interested party in any manner DOE determines is appropriate, including, but not limited to, the creation of a competitive solicitation. Interested parties should not include any classified, business confidential, and/or proprietary information in their responses. DOE personnel may contact parties responding to this notification to clarify responses as part of this market research process. DOE is committed to ensuring a fair, full and open, collaborative, and transparent solicitation process. Future information regarding the solicitation, including questions and answers, if appropriate, will be posted on the competition website at https://science.osti.gov/Acquisition-Management/ContractCompetitions. This website will be the primary distribution medium used to disseminate information relating to this competition as it becomes available. Offerors are responsible for frequently monitoring the website for information, notices, and updates regarding the solicitation. DOE looks forward to engaging with the community, industry, and other interested parties in a transparent and collaborative manner throughout the solicitation process for a contractor to manage ORISE. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO AWARD A CONTRACT AT THIS TIME.
